doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: Master classes and the manual using Arban
summary: He says he wants to spare students his wasted effort, and explains his manual and Arban page 93 keyed by the week.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: After that, after than, and you know when I do master classes it’s the same thing. I’ll go in and I’ll say, “You want to sound like that? This is what you do to fix that.” And they try it and they go, “That’s pretty good.” Well how did I know how to fix that? That’s what I used to do. I said, “All the things that you all are doing,” I said, “I used to do.” So don’t think that I’m some sort of a savant or something. I said, “I just spent an extraordinary amount of time wasted trying to figure out how to do it right.” And I said, “And I’m glad I did it, because I don’t want you to do that. I want to be a catalytic person in your life. I want you to skip all the bad things that I did to try to learn how to play the trumpet.” I said, like for instance, like the book that I wrote, it’s not a book, it’s just a manual for the students to read about how the trumpet works and stuff like that. But I don’t want, most of the books that I’ve ever gotten/bought, I have every book known to man. Like I said, I have 15,000 entries in my library at home. So I’ve got a lot of books and pieces. I said, “You know most of them don’t have much writing in them at all, they just, you know like play these magic etudes and you’ll be better.” No. You’ll be better at playing the way you play and hopefully getting half the notes and still sounding bad. So I said, so the book that I wrote, everything in that book, if you play it wrong it sounds bad. It’s just going to sound bad. From the beginning to the end, it’s one technique. But nobody knows that. They’re just trying to learn all these new materials and I’m working on the same thing every lesson using the materials to fine tune what I should be talking to them about. Because once again, the materials are remedial to start and then after we get along I can even give them more stuff, they get less entries in the lesson thing that are longer, but they’re longer. See? So you start out with short things they can do. [scats] You know Arban ’93. Yeah. So the old ’93. Now I don’t even know what pages are anymore, they have all different pages in these 30 Arban books. You know? So and you © Fillius Jazz Archive -23-

can complete the C and G line on that page. That’s all you have to do. C and G. So it’s a discipline study. You have seven elements that you get tested on, and they’re all — sometimes a page, sometimes a half a page, sometimes one line, two lines off a full page in all the keys. So they’re always doing page 93, 125, and 142. They’re always doing that, every week, but only two of the keys. So they learn the whole thing by the end of the semester rather than say okay I want you to learn all of page 93. They can’t play in half of those keys. They’re going to just hate trumpet, they’re going to hate taking lessons. And if they practice, they won’t because they catch up to the ones that don’t practice that are already can play those things. They think they can.
